subject: Discovery recap: FinBot — inference cost pressure
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@finbot.ai>, Tina Matthews <tina@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: FinBot — inference cost pressure

Hi Carlos / Tina —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have shared clarity and can move to a focused technical deep-dive with Ben next week.

What we heard (pain / context):
- Main pressure: per-inference unit economics — current infra costs are eating into margin as you scale to multi-million monthly requests.
- Current stack: models hosted in AWS SageMaker with a Triton front-end; single-replica endpoints for some latency-sensitive traffic, batch jobs for non-critical ranking.
- Typical request profile: median prompt ~250 tokens, median response ~120 tokens; bursty traffic around payroll run and peak market hours.
- Latency target: 95th < 300ms for interactive features; acceptable background batch latency up to 10s.
- Key constraints: cannot tolerate model-quality regression (finance domain), but open to quantization if we can verify parity on evals.

Success criteria (what a good outcome looks like):
1) Reduce per-token inference cost by 2x (or equivalent ops cost reduction) while meeting 95th/99th latency goals.
2) Predictable cost model for budgeting (monthly committed vs burst).
3) No regression on the 10-benchmark prompt set you shared; formal eval gating before rollouts.

What Redwood can help with (next-level summary):
- Serving performance: our runtime reduces per-token GPU time via continuous batching and KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Cost controls: recommendations on batching, cache policies, and quantization profiles tailored to your model family.
- Safe rollouts: canary/on-demand fallback to larger models if quality drops.

Immediate next steps agreed:
- Tech deep-dive: Ben to run an architecture review + perf simulation; please include your infra diagrams and a representative sample of 1h request logs (anonymized).
- We'll run a rough unit-economics estimate based on your traffic profile and provide an initial cost delta (Redwood-hosted vs your current setup).
- Share our pricing & MAP (attached) and propose a pilot plan for a single high-value endpoint.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Time options: I sent a Calendly link for Ben below — if those don't work, tell us a couple of windows and we'll accommodate.

Thanks — talk soon.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

PS: If you can share a sample of your 95th/99th latency measurements and a 7-day request histogram before the deep-dive, that will help us size batching & cache expectations.

From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@finbot.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinBot — inference cost pressure

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap, looks accurate. A few clarifications / requests before we lock the deep-dive: 
- Throughput: baseline is ~200 req/s average, with spikes up to ~1.2k req/s for a 10–15 minute window during peak.
- Current 95th: roughly 420ms (tail suffers during bursts). We can export 1 week of traces and the 10 prompt eval set you mentioned.
- Quantization: engineering is open but wants to see end-to-end evals; we cannot accept >1% F1 degradation on our compliance prompts.

Ben — can you include a short checklist of infra artifacts you need so we bundle the right logs/configs?

Two scheduling notes: 1) Calendly slot at 11am PT on Monday looks good, I booked it. 2) For the pilot, we prefer starting with a single non-critical endpoint that drives <10% of traffic.

—Carlos
VP Product, FinBot
carlos@finbot.ai

On Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 4:05 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (see recap below)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinBot — inference cost pressure

Thanks Carlos — great context, and appreciate booking the Monday slot. A couple of quick notes / answers before Ben's deep-dive: 

- Checklist for artifacts (Ben):
  1) 1 week request logs (anonymized) + request/response sizes
  2) 95th/99th latency histograms for peak and off-peak windows
  3) Model details: family (e.g., LLaMA-2 13B), tokenization, current quantization (if any)
  4) Deployment config: instance types, autoscaling policies, and any custom Triton config

- Pilot approach: agree on starting with a single non-critical endpoint (<=10% traffic). We'll run an A/B with prefix caching enabled and compare cost/latency and run evals on your benchmark set.

- Quantization plan: we can provide a small eval harness to test int8 (or Q4_0) on your prompts — Ben will include pass/fail gates. If you prefer, we can run parallel runs to confirm no >1% F1 drop.

I've attached the pricing sheet + MAP again; Ben will follow up with a technical agenda for Monday's deep-dive.

Links: Tech deep-dive slot (https://calendly.com/ben-carter/tech-deep-dive), shared notes (https://drive.google.com/finbot-demo-notes)

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx
